actions.reason:
Reduces per-call overhead on the encode paths without changing outputs.
1. RegexTokenizer.encode with special tokens no longer builds and compiles an alternation regex (pure-Python regex parser) on every call. When all special tokens are non-empty strings, the text is split with str.find: the leftmost occurrence wins, and at equal positions the token listed first wins, the same as the regex alternation. The result list has the same layout as re.split with a capturing group. Other cases still use re.split.
2. encode_ordinary calls self.compiled_pattern.findall(text) directly instead of going through the module-level regex.findall wrapper.
3. BasicTokenizer.encode keeps the sorted (pair string, replacement char) list and the result of the merge validity check. They are recomputed only when the merges object or its length changes, the same staleness rule as the existing merge lookup cache. Before, it re-sorted and re-validated all merges on every call.
Measured: encode_ir ratio 0.9895, train_ir 1.0056 (within guard), outputs identical in the equivalence harness.

journal.text:
I changed RegexTokenizer.encode in minbpe/regex.py so that special tokens no longer build and compile an alternation regex on every call. When all special tokens are non-empty strings, the text is split with str.find. The leftmost occurrence wins, and at equal positions the first listed token wins. I also edited the encode path in minbpe/basic.py.

Evaluation 1 was rejected. encode_ir went from 410004018 to 408076012, ratio 0.9953 against a required 0.9900. Evaluation 3 was also rejected, at ratio 0.9950. Evaluation 5 touched both files, 60 lines, and was accepted. encode_ir went from 409947466 to 405643035, ratio 0.9895. train_ir rose to ratio 1.0056. Outputs were identical in every run.

The regex.py change alone did not clear the threshold. The basic.py change was needed. The gain is small and close to the limit.

Wait for the replay verdict. Then look at why train_ir rose about half a percent, and at other per-call overhead in encode_ordinary.
